title: The 7 Best AI To-Do List Apps for 2026
summary: We compared the best AI to-do list apps for 2026 on prioritization, scheduling and price, so you can pick the one that actually keeps you on top of work.
body_markdown:
Most to-do lists fail the same way. You add tasks faster than you finish them, the list turns into a graveyard, and the things that matter get buried under the things that were easy to write down.


The best AI to-do list apps try to fix that. Some schedule your tasks onto your calendar. Some turn a rambling voice note into a clean list. A few go further and build the list for you by reading the email, Slack threads and meetings where your work actually shows up.


We looked at seven of them.


Below you'll find what each one does well, where it falls short, what it costs (checked against each pricing page in October 2026) and who it's for.


## Key takeaways


-


**BOND** is the pick if your tasks live in email, Slack and meetings. It builds and reprioritizes the list for you, which is why busy executives use it.


-


**Motion** and **Reclaim** are the strongest options if you want AI to fit your tasks into your calendar.


-


**Todoist** and **TickTick** are the best value if you're happy adding tasks yourself and just want smart help on top.


## The quick list


1.


**BOND** : a self-updating to-do list that pulls tasks from your tools, ranks them for you, and updates as you work.


2.


**Motion** : auto-schedules tasks and projects into your calendar.


3.


**Todoist** : the classic list app, now with voice capture and AI task help.


4.


**Sunsama** : a calm, guided daily planning ritual for people who want strong routine.


5.


**Akiflow** : one inbox for tasks from every tool, plus time blocking.


6.


**Reclaim** : AI calendar that defends time for tasks, habits and focus.


7.


**TickTick** : a cheap, feature-packed list app with a built-in focus timer.


## How we evaluated these AI to-do list apps


We judged each app on five things:


-


**Capture.** How do tasks get in? Typing, voice, integrations, or automatically?


-


**Prioritization.** Does the AI help you decide what matters, or just store what you tell it?


-


**Accuracy.** When the app makes a call for you, is it right often enough to trust?


-


**Effort.** How much daily upkeep does it need to stay useful?


-


**Price.** What you pay, verified on each pricing page.


The biggest split turned out to be capture. Most apps on this list still depend on you to notice a task and write it down. That's the step where things slip.


## 1. BOND


*The to-do list that updates itself.*


BOND connects to the tools where your work already happens (Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion and more) and turns what it finds into one prioritized to-do list. A contract waiting for your signature, an investor email you owe a reply, a teammate who reported a bug: each becomes a task tagged P0 to P3, and the list updates as you work.


It learns your priorities over time, so what rises to the top reflects what actually matters to you, not just what's newest. It's built for executives and leaders who get pulled in a dozen directions a day, and users consistently say the same thing about it: it cuts through the noise. If you've ever wondered[how to prioritize tasks when everything is P0,](https://www.bondapp.io/insights/how-to-prioritize-tasks-when-everything-is-p0) this is the tool built around that problem.


**Key features**


-


Self-updating to-do list built from email, Slack, calendar and docs


-


Automatic follow-up and commitment tracking (including what you're waiting on from others)


-


A morning brief with who's waiting on you and what deserves your attention


-


Meeting prep briefs and follow-up drafts written in your voice


-


Lives in Slack and iMessage, so there's no new app to check


-


Custom routines for recurring work


**What works:** You stop being the one who has to notice every task. Because BOND reads the source (the email, the thread, the meeting), its priorities are extremely accurate, and nothing depends on you remembering to write it down.


**Limitations:** It's the most expensive option here, and it's built around work tools, so it's not the place for a grocery list. If you just want a simple personal checklist, a cheaper app will do.


**Pricing:** Free to start with 10,000 credits. The individual plan is $49/month. Enterprise is custom.


**Best for:** Executives, founders and chiefs of staff whose tasks arrive through email, Slack and meetings. (Curious how it compares to a human hire? See what an[AI chief of staff actually is](https://www.bondapp.io/insights/what-is-an-ai-chief-of-staff) .)


## 2. Motion


*Your task list, auto-scheduled into your calendar.*


Motion takes your tasks, deadlines and priorities and fits them into your calendar automatically. When a meeting moves or a task runs long, it reshuffles everything else.


It has grown into a broader work platform with AI projects, docs, notes and meeting tools, so it suits teams that want one place to plan.


**Key features**


-


AI task planner that builds your schedule for you


-


Projects, Gantt timelines and team capacity planning (Business plan)


-


AI docs, notes and meeting features


**What works:** If your problem is "I have the list but never find time to do it," Motion's auto-scheduling is the real deal.


**Limitations:** You still have to get every task into Motion yourself. The broader platform also means more to learn than a simple list.


**Pricing:** Pro AI from $19/seat/month and Business AI from $29/seat/month, with a free trial. Annual billing saves 33%.


**Best for:** People and small teams who want their whole day time-blocked for them.


## 3. Todoist


*The reliable classic, with AI on top.*


Todoist has been a favorite list app for years, and its natural language input is still the best around. Type "send board update every Friday at 9am" and it sets the due date and repeat for you.


Its AI features are practical. Ramble lets you talk through what's on your mind and turns it into tasks. Task Assist on paid plans helps break vague tasks into concrete steps.


**What works:** Fast, clean and available everywhere. It's hard to find a more dependable list app.


**Limitations:** Todoist doesn't decide what's important for you. You set priorities by hand, and every task still starts with you typing or speaking it.


**Pricing:** Free plan with limited Ramble sessions. Pro is $5/month billed yearly ($7 monthly). Business is $8/user/month billed yearly ($10 monthly).


**Best for:** Anyone who wants a fast, trusted list with light AI help.


## 4. Sunsama


*A calm daily plan instead of an endless list.*


Sunsama is built around a daily planning ritual. Each morning it walks you through what you'll work on, pulls in tasks from tools like Asana, Jira and email, and asks you to be realistic about how much fits in a day.


It's less about AI doing the work and more about a better habit, with AI and MCP support added on the paid plan.


**What works:** It's the antidote to overcommitting. Many people find the guided shutdown at the end of the day just as useful as the morning plan.


**Limitations:** The ritual takes 10 to 15 minutes a day, and you choose every task yourself. If you want the app to make decisions for you, this isn't it.


**Pricing:** Pro is $17/month billed yearly or $22 billed monthly, with a 14-day free trial (no card needed).


**Best for:** People who feel scattered and want a mindful planning routine.


## 5. Akiflow


*One inbox for every task, wherever it came from.*


Akiflow collects tasks from your email, Slack, Notion and other tools into a single inbox, then lets you drag them onto your calendar to time block. Its AI assistant, Aki, can help plan and manage tasks through chat.


**Key features**


-


Universal inbox across your tools


-


Calendar time blocking with keyboard shortcuts


-


Aki AI assistant and MCP connector


**What works:** Power users love how fast it is. Getting tasks from ten tools into one place is a big step up from scattered lists.


**Limitations:** Akiflow gathers things for you, but you still triage the inbox and decide what's a priority. No free plan, and the AI meeting assistant is a $19/month add-on.


**Pricing:** Pro is $19/month billed yearly or $34 monthly, with a 7-day trial (card required).


**Best for:** Keyboard-first professionals who want to time block everything.


## 6. Reclaim


*An AI calendar that protects time for your tasks.*


Reclaim, now part of Dropbox, works inside Google Calendar and Outlook. You give it tasks, habits and focus time goals, and it finds and defends the time on your calendar, moving blocks around as meetings change.


**What works:** It has a generous free tier and plays nicely with the calendar you already use. Great for protecting focus time from a meeting-heavy week.


**Limitations:** It's a calendar tool first. Tasks still need to be added (or synced from another app), and it doesn't judge which ones matter most.


**Pricing:** Free Lite plan. Starter is $10/seat/month billed yearly ($12 monthly), Business is $15 ($18 monthly), and Enterprise is $22, billed yearly only.


**Best for:** Teams on Google or Outlook who want tasks and focus time scheduled automatically.


## 7. TickTick


*The most features for the lowest price.*


TickTick packs a lot into one app: lists, calendar views, a Pomodoro focus timer and a habit tracker. Natural language input sets dates and reminders as you type.


Its AI features are lighter than others here. Think of it as a great list app with some smart touches rather than an AI-first tool.


**What works:** Premium costs less than $5 a month and replaces two or three other apps.


**Limitations:** Prioritizing is fully manual, and the free plan caps you at 9 lists.


**Pricing:** Free plan available. Premium is $49.99/year.


**Best for:** Students and budget-conscious users who want everything in one place.


## Which of the best AI to-do list apps is right for you?


Start with where your tasks come from.


If they arrive in email, Slack and meetings, and your real problem is keeping track of it all, **BOND** is the one that builds and ranks the list for you. Nothing else here does that end to end.


If you already know your tasks but can't find time to do them, pick **Motion** for full auto-scheduling or **Reclaim** if you want to stay inside Google Calendar or Outlook.


Want structure and calm? **Sunsama** . Want speed and one inbox? **Akiflow** .


And if you just need a solid list without spending much, **Todoist** or **TickTick** will serve you well for years.


Still weighing an assistant against a task app? Our roundup of[the best AI executive assistants](https://www.bondapp.io/insights/8-best-ai-executive-assistants-for-busy-leaders-in-2026) covers the next step up.


## FAQ


**What are the best AI to-do list apps in 2026?**


For executives and busy leaders, BOND is our top pick because it builds your list from email, Slack and meetings. Motion and Reclaim lead for AI scheduling, and Todoist and TickTick are the best value list apps.


**Can an AI to-do list prioritize tasks for me?**


Some can. Most apps let you set priorities by hand and help schedule them. BOND ranks tasks for you (P0 to P3) based on what it sees across your tools and learns your priorities over time.


**Is there a free AI to-do list app?**


Yes. Todoist, TickTick and Reclaim all have free plans, and BOND offers 10,000 free credits to start. Free tiers usually limit AI usage or features.


**What's the difference between an AI to-do list and an AI scheduler?**


An AI to-do list helps you decide what to do. An AI scheduler like Motion or Reclaim decides when to do it by placing tasks on your calendar. Some people use one of each.


**Are AI to-do list apps safe to connect to my email?**


Check each vendor's security page before connecting work accounts. Look for SOC 2 compliance, clear data retention terms and the option to disconnect at any time.


**Can an AI to-do list replace an executive assistant?**


For task tracking and follow-ups, it can cover a lot of ground. For judgment calls and relationships, people still matter. Our guide to[chief of staff vs executive assistant](https://www.bondapp.io/insights/chief-of-staff-vs-executive-assistant) breaks down where each role fits.
